plate.subject: a crowded crossroads market of many kinds of men

paragraphs.text: Men are Common Folk, mortal like the dwarves. They lived in Aoaz in great numbers, generation after generation, for thousands of years before the First Age. The earliest of them were stronger, longer-lived and more gifted in magic than the men of later ages.

sources.section: First Age ethnic and political history

paragraphs.text: Many peoples of men live in Aoaz: the peoples of the Middle Kingdom, the Dondor Brutes, the camel warriors of Noris, the clans of Gunwaith, the wardens of Girdon, the Buldor companies, the houses of Aenor Isle and the Goodin Sunfolk. The ancient Ainu, the First Men, stand at the head of their story.
From Aen, who was born of magic and had no ordinary father, came the highest royal line of men. His victory in the War of Men and the founding of Aenor began the First Age.

sources.section: First Age ethnic and political history

paragraphs.text: Men have fought on both sides of the great wars. In the First Age men of the eastern and southern lands marched with Volgan, while the western kingdoms and the island peoples joined the Grand Alliance against him. No people of men served him whole.

sources.section: First Age ethnic and political history

paragraphs.text: Beside men live the small folk, a people of their own. Their own name for themselves and the place of their homeland are not set down in the chronicles of men.

plate.subject: tall ancient men in a ruined hall of giant stones

paragraphs.text: Men had built civilizations for thousands of years before the First Age began. The earliest generations were stronger than later men, lived far longer, and were naturally better at magic. Some of them held powers like those of gods, without being true gods.

sources.section: The Ainu and the First Men

paragraphs.text: Aen was born from magic and power, without an ordinary father. He is called the First Man and First of His Name, though he was not the first man to live. The title speaks of his unique birth and of his place as founder of the one realm of men.

sources.section: The Ainu and the First Men

paragraphs.text: Aen lived an extraordinarily long life and fathered hundreds of sons. He fought in the War of Men for centuries, united the rival kingdoms of men into one kingdom, and founded Aenor. His victory marks the first year of the First Age. His blood is held the most royal of all mankind, and he is widely held to be the greatest man who ever lived.

sources.section: The Ainu and the First Men

paragraphs.text: The old peoples of that early world are called the Ainu. The scholars do not agree whether the name means all the mighty men of the early world, only the dynasty of Aen, or a people older still. No chronicle tells where Aen first appeared, or what power brought about his birth.

sources.section: The Ainu and the First Men

paragraphs.text: Aen, the magically born founder of Aenor and First of His Name, fathered hundreds of sons. His blood is held the most royal of all mankind.

His many sons and their descendants made many royal lines, and those lines have long competed with one another. How the Golden King and the kings of the Restoration descend from Aen is not set down in any chronicle.
Among the sons of Aen was Ein. The chronicles count the direct line of Aen through Ein as the first royal line of men, and they have long held it lost. Why it was held lost, no chronicle tells.
paragraphs.note: Reading the line held lost as the line of Ein follows the descent the vault gives; the reason it was held lost is open.

paragraphs.text: Ein’s line has returned. The stranger from the ice is Eindil, son of Ein, grandson of Aen. His descent from the founder of Aenor is direct, an unusually strong claim of blood, though it gives him no lawful rule over the crowns of the West and the North that stand apart from Aenor.
Eindil lived through the ages in a long sleep beyond nature. Where and how he was put to sleep, no chronicle tells.

sources.section: The Ainu and the First Men

paragraphs.text: Ein had two sons, born at about the same time: Eindil and Afrit. Ein denied Afrit the throne. Why he refused him, which of the brothers was the elder, and who their mother was, no chronicle tells.
Afrit survived the ages through magic and corruption. Under another name he was hailed as a New God and worshipped throughout Aenor.

sources.section: The Ainu and the First Men

plate.subject: an elven council under great trees

paragraphs.text: The elves of the Magical Forest are Great Folk, immortal beings who are not spirits. They are peaceful and very old, and their forest is the oldest and most peaceful of the elven realms of the Magical Lands, beyond the Great Wall of Aenor. An elected council of its houses rules it.
paragraphs.note: The elected council of houses is proposed.

paragraphs.text: Around the Magical Forest lie some twenty smaller elven realms. Herrodon and Andos Enda are old rivals, and Nolorim guards the high passes. The elves of the Magical Lands were never conquered, not even by Elzon. The elven powers can command the dragons of Dragon Mountain.
In the First Age the elves of the Magical Lands fought in the Grand Alliance against Volgan. Not every elf stood with them: corrupted elves marched in Volgan’s army.

sources.section: First Age ethnic and political history

paragraphs.text: King Edran’s attack on the Ember Lands after Dardan cost many elven lives and left elves and men long estranged. When Elzon invaded Aenor in the Second Age, the elven kingdoms would not help. That refusal still stands.

plate.subject: very tall elves on white-gold terraces

paragraphs.text: The Sunhot elves live in the Lands of the Sun, in the far south-west of Aoaz. They stand more than three metres tall, and they are among the strongest and the most peaceful peoples of Aoaz. Like all elves they are Great Folk, immortal beings who are not spirits.
Their land is divided among many small realms, which the Lands of Light lead.
In the same lands the Gala elves keep their ancient court. Whether the Gala are kin to the Sunhot elves, no chronicle of men can say.

sources.section: First Age ethnic and political history

plate.subject: an ancient white court in southern light

paragraphs.text: The Gala elves are the people of King Lorien. They keep their ancient court in the Lands of the Sun, and they are the most powerful of all elves.

Lorien is a figure of extraordinary age and power, with eyes that glow a bright yellow and robes of gold and white. In the First Age he led the Gala elves in King Edran’s Grand Alliance, and they fought against Volgan at Dardan. Lorien has lived through every age since. He remembers the War of Men, the defeat of Volgan at Dardan, the collapse of Aenor and the reign of Elzon.

sources.section: First Age ethnic and political history

paragraphs.text: The Gala elves remember Edran’s Folly, the attack on the Ember Lands after Dardan that brought needless elven deaths and a long estrangement between elves and men. They would not go to war again for Aenor against Elzon. Even so, Lorien’s care is for the fate of all Aoaz.
Whether the Gala are kin to the Sunhot elves, no chronicle of men can say.

sources.section: First Age ethnic and political history

paragraphs.text: Lorien is dead. He fell in the war at the end of the Fourth Age, fighting for all the living peoples of Aoaz, and the Gala elves lost the king who had led them since the First Age.

The God Forest Keepers are elves, and like all elves they are Great Folk, immortal beings who are not spirits. The chronicles of men name them beside the elves of the Magical Forest, the Sunhot elves and the Gala elves.
Little more is written of them. No chronicle of men tells where the forest they keep lies, what their keeping means, or how they stand toward the other elven peoples.

plate.subject: Netherborn on a volcanic pass, seen far off

paragraphs.text: Angels are Great Folk, immortal beings who are not spirits. Their history is not written in any chronicle of men.
Demons are corrupted angels. Among them are the Shachihata, huge, powerful and rare, and the Netherborn, who serve Volgan. Whether all the demonic peoples share one corruption is not known.
The King of Demons has his seat in the Nether, in the south of the Ember Lands, and no chronicle gives his name. His pacts bind the living, but the souls of the dead remain Zol’s.

In the Second Age portals opened, demons came forth, and they raided Aenor and other peoples. Agon and other demons were active in the Nether. What place Agon holds among the demons of the Nether is not known.

Devils are not demons. They are corrupted Lesser Spirits, ancient and terrible, and they are bound to their bodies; the elves say they fled a service older than Aoaz, and the chronicles of men do not. A slain devil returns only through the lava rite, performed with its skull; who performs it, and where, is not known. Demonic signs include the five-pointed star.
South of the South Lands, beyond the lands that anyone has charted, lie the homes of devils, demons and other evil beings that live in fire and endless suffering. They are known by name only.
Afrit has demons of his own. Whether they share one corruption with the Netherborn and the Shachihata is not known.

The dwarves are Common Folk and mortal, like men. They hold the great mountain ranges of the West Lands and the North Lands, and the range of the Great Wall of Aenor between the Middle Lands and the Magical Lands.
In the First Age dwarves joined the Grand Alliance against Volgan. Where the dwarves first dwelt, no chronicle tells.

sources.section: First Age ethnic and political history

paragraphs.text: The dwarf goblins of the hills of the North Lands, near Lerendor, are another people altogether. They are neither dwarves nor goblins, but a people of their own.

Several peoples of giants live in Aoaz. In the Middle Lands lies Hirolon, a sovereign kingdom of giants. It is not one of Aenor’s chartered dominions, and it treats with Aenor from outside the Charters.
paragraphs.note: The Charters of Parim are proposed; Hirolon as a sovereign giant kingdom that treats with Aenor is established.

sources.section: The Middle Lands: Aenor and the Concord

paragraphs.text: In the Cold Lands live the ice giants of Titanos. Others are called the Forgotten Giants. In the First Age giants joined the Grand Alliance against Volgan.

sources.section: First Age ethnic and political history

paragraphs.text: To which order of being the giants belong, whether they are mortal, and where they first came from, is not known.

plate.subject: tree-folk walking through a misty forest

paragraphs.text: The ents are the people of Kilinti Forest in the Middle Lands. Kilinti is one of the dominions of the Middle Kingdom Concord, and its ents keep their own lords under the Charters of Parim.
paragraphs.note: The Charters of Parim as the frame of the dominions are proposed.

sources.section: The Middle Lands: Aenor and the Concord

paragraphs.text: The ents are not the only walking tree folk. Aenor Forest, the largest forest of the Middle Lands, is home to a walking tree people separate from the ents, whose own name the chronicles of men have not recorded. Ents and the walking tree people never share a forest.
To which order of being the ents belong, and whether they are mortal, is not known.

The yeti live in the Yeti Lands of the Cold Lands, in the north-west of Aoaz. The Cold Lands are the largest landmass of Aoaz and the least known, and they reach west and north beyond the known lands.

Like the tribes, the ice giants of Titanos and the free towns of the coast, the yeti of the Cold Lands live by trade, herding and hunting. To which order of being they belong, and whether they are mortal, is not known.
paragraphs.note: The ways of life of the Cold Lands peoples are proposed.

paragraphs.text: The mycids are the people of the Mushroom Forest in the Magical Lands, east of the Great Wall of Aenor. The arcanists are the people of the Zhen Hills.
Little more of either people is written in the chronicles of men. To which order of being the mycids and the arcanists belong, whether they are mortal, and where they first came from, is not known.

plate.subject: orc and goblin warbands at a hold gate

paragraphs.text: Orcs and goblins live in many lands of Aoaz, in many realms and under many rulers. They are not one obedient people. Like the other monster peoples of Aoaz, they are independent and diverse, and no single master commands them all.

In the Dark Lands, Goldoroth, an orc kingdom, seeks to rule the whole region, and a dozen orc and goblin holds belong to nobody. Volgan’s agents court them all, but most still answer only to themselves.
Goblins avoid the deep cold, yet they hold sheltered valleys in the south of the Cold Lands. The hobgoblin king rules his own realm only, not every goblin.
After Dardan, orcs and goblins loyal to Volgan and Elzon went on raiding through the early Second Age, while the Dark Lands fell back into chaos.
Trolls and ogres live in the Dark Lands under rulers of their own, beside independent men, orcs, goblins, giants and demons. The Troll Forest of the Dark Lands belongs to nobody.
Smash, a troll king, rules his own realm only, not every troll. Like the other monster peoples, trolls and ogres are not one obedient people, and not all of them serve Volgan.
To which order of being trolls and ogres belong, and whether they are mortal, is not known.

plate.subject: mist over barrows, figures far away

paragraphs.text: Grave hosts and undead walk in more than one land of Aoaz. To which order of being, if any, the ghosts, revenants and roaming dead belong, the scholars do not agree.

In the Second Age Elzon, the Great Necromancer, raised the dead on a huge scale, among them the fallen fighters of Aenor, so that his armies grew as his enemies lost men. He borrowed ancient magic linked to Zol to do it, and how he came by that magic is not known.

The dead that Elzon raised faded with time and needed his magic to go on. His power waned when he stayed in Aenor, far from the Ember Lands that sustained it, and in the Magical Lands Varner, a Lesser Spirit, could lift the curse of the dead.

sources.section: Third Age limitations and permanent death

paragraphs.text: The dead also roam the black wastes of Zol’s Mistake. They have no known kind or allegiance, and no chronicle tells whether they all belong to Zol, to Volgan or to any one master.
The scholars do not agree whether raising a body commands its true soul, whether souls are held at all, or whether only bodies and memories are used.
paragraphs.note: Raising a body is not command of its soul is a proposed rule; whether souls are held is open.

paragraphs.text: Zol’s dead have risen beyond the Mistake. They are stronger than any corpse Elzon raised, for the Old God’s own death-magic sustains them. Mortal arms cannot end them for good without magic.
Dragons come chiefly from Dragon Mountain. They do not form a realm of their own, and the elven powers can command them.
In the First Age dragons fought in Volgan’s army, beside demons, devils, monsters, Great Spirits and damned spirits. That does not mean that every dragon served him.

sources.section: First Age ethnic and political history

paragraphs.text: The elves of the Magical Lands have entrusted a dragon to the Man from the Ice, as an ally in the war.
In the Abyss of the Ember Lands dwells a people of large humanoids with the heads of rhinoceroses. Roka, whose name is bound to the Abyss, is one of them.
Roka is linked with the Necklace of the Abyss, a relic of great power. Whether he guarded it himself, why it holds such power, and how it stands toward his people, no chronicle tells.
The name of his people, their history and their way of life are not known. The Abyss is not the Void that held Volgan, nor the Nether of the King of Demons, and how such places may join is not known.
